q: How does a Tiruppur knitwear unit work out carbon per garment?
title: Tiruppur knitwear: carbon per garment
short: Add the unit's electricity and fuel emissions for the month and divide by pieces packed. That gives the making-stage figure per garment. Fabric, yarn and dyeing bought in sit in Scope 3 and should be added from supplier figures, not guessed.
audience: Knitwear and garment units in the Tiruppur cluster of Tamil Nadu

p: Electricity kWh x 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh.
Diesel for generators in litres x 2.68 kg CO2 per litre.
Add, then divide by pieces packed in the month.
If products differ a lot, split by standard minutes per piece instead of piece count, and state the basis.

example.title: Worked example: one month (illustrative inputs)
lines: Generator diesel: 840 L x 2.68 = 2,251.2 kg CO2
Pieces packed: 100,000, so 20,001.2 / 100,000 = 0.200 kg CO2 per piece
example.note: Quantities are illustrative; use your bills and packing register.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
